messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] service=runtime-proxy severity=page — queue_depth > 9000 for 3m, tokens_throttled spikes detected :rotating_light:
ashley: paging oncall — I'm seeing queue depth and throttle graphs go vertical, users experiencing 503s.
sam: oncall here, looking. any customer-facing incidents flagged?
maria: support flagged 2 high-priority customers seeing timeouts ~10:12 UTC.
kevin: adding context — autoscaler HPA hasn't spun extra pods, cpu% low but queue_depth high. Maybe metric mismatch.
ashley: exactly, our queue_depth aggregator looks like it undercounts when sharded, so autoscaler didn't trigger.
ashley: can we triage: 1) mitigate customer impact 2) get more capacity 3) fix alerting + autoscale rule
sam: mitigation step 1: enable manual-scale on the affected runtime pool to +5 pods. Doing now: `kubectl scale deploy/runtime-pool-3 --replicas=12`
incident-bot: action triggered by sam: scaled runtime-pool-3 to 12 replicas.
kevin: seeing backlog drain slowly, tokens/sec still high ~14k across pool. Throttles tick down as new pods warm.
maria: notifying support to update customers — ETA ~6m for degradation to stop. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
ashley: good. while we stabilize, let's adjust alerts so noise doesn't keep paging. Current alert fires on `sum(queue_depth)>9000` for 3m, but that spikes on transient back pressure.
sam: agree. propose changing primary paging alert to combine tokens/sec and sustained throttle count. Something like:
```
ALERT AutoScaleCapacityCritical
IF sum(rate(request_tokens_total[1m])) by (pool) > 12000
AND increase(throttle_events_total[5m]) > 50
FOR 2m
```
kevin: also add a fallback: if queue_depth > 11000 for 5m then page. Keeps long tail.
ashley: let's implement a staging change: reduce pages from queue_depth and route initial pages to secondary oncall (paging severity=warning). Then only escalate to primary if combined rule fires.
incident-bot: sam updated alert config in staging (pr 4821).
sam: rolling the change to staging dashboards and alertmanager now.
maria: while we're changing alerts, can we add a small dashboard panel showing `tokens/sec per shard` and `queue_depth per shard` — previous dashboards only showed aggregated totals, which hid skew.
kevin: good call. running quick PromQLs to illustrate skew:
```
# tokens per shard
sum(rate(request_tokens_total[1m])) by (shard)
# queue depth per shard
sum(queue_depth) by (shard)
```
ashley: I'm going to create a synthetic probe hitting the public endpoint at 10r/s to detect latency degradation pre-autoscale. We should add it as a Canary signal for the autoscaler to use.
sam: +1. Also note HPA uses custom metric `queue_depth_per_pod` derived from aggregated queue_depth / replicas — that's the problem: shard variance causes mask. We should feed per-pod queue depth or tokens/sec into the HPA instead.
kevin: created an issue: GH #3456 — "HPA should use per-pod tokens/sec metric, not global aggregate". tagging runtime and autoscale teams.
ashley: action items we agreed: 1) change alert rules in prod to combined rule (sam) 2) add shard-level panels to ops dashboard (maria) 3) update autoscaler config to use per-pod tokens/sec (kevin) 4) add synthetic probe and wire to SLO alerts (ashley) 5) update runbook with new thresholds and handoff steps (sam + maria).
maria: I've opened a dashboard PR with the two panels and added an explanation note. PR 2189.
sam: rolling alert changes to prod in 5m window to avoid flapping. will set mute windows for existing queue_depth alert while experiment runs.
incident-bot: prod alert silence created for `queue_depth > 9000` for 30m by sam.
kevin: after scaling, throttle events are down to baseline. Visible customer errors decreasing.
maria: support confirmed two customers got transient 503s but recovery succeeded and no persistent data loss.
ashley: thank you. keep monitoring for 30m, then we'll start implementing autoscaler fix.
kevin: quick note — autoscaler logs show `metric-not-found` errors for 3 pods; collector had a transient network partition to metrics backend. I'll include that in postmortem.
sam: putting this in incident mode for 45m so we can finish changes. tagging infra and runtime to review HPA change.
maria: starting customer postmortem draft in docs: https://redwood-internal/incident/1764567890 — adding timeline and support notes.
ashley: once HPA change PR is up, please include benchmark: heavy sequential tokens/sec load and show scaling events with per-pod metric. Need numbers before next oncall rotation.
kevin: will run a local sim and attach graphs. planning to use `wrk` + a small harness to push token-heavy requests.
sam: final: update runbook snippet with new combined alert rule and example PromQL. I'll paste into runbook tonight.
ashley: thanks team. great coordination. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: incident mode ended by sam. Duration 48m.
ashley: follow-up sync at 15:00 UTC in #eng-runtime to review autoscaler PR and dashboards.
maria: adding link to the dashboard PR and incident notes in the ticket.
kevin: noting next steps in GH #3456 and assigning to @sam for review.
ashley: closing thread after postmortem complete. Please ping if anything else pops up. :pray:
